Subject:  Professional Services Agreement with Quinto Consulting LP for City
  Treasurer Services

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Provide a recommendation to the City Council to appoint
Ruth Quinto of Quinto Consulting LP to serve as Treasurer and 2) to enter into a
professional services agreement with Quinto Consulting LP for Treasury Services for a
three-year term.

FISCAL IMPACT: No additional appropriation is required. Funding in the amount of
$40,000 for the initial year of this three-year agreement is included in the Adopted Budget
for FY 2026-27 in Account No. 100-7054-5100-00. Beginning with the second contract
year, and on each anniversary thereafter, the annual not-to-exceed compensation may be
increased by up to three percent (3%) for a total contract amount of $123,636. Funding for
subsequent years will be budgeted accordingly through the annual budget process.

STRATEGIC PLAN IMPLEMENTATION: N/A

DISCUSSION: Section 2.16.010 of the Malibu Municipal Code (MMC) states, in part, that
“the City Council shall appoint a City Treasurer who shall be responsible for the safe
deposit of all moneys in the custody of the City and shall perform all the duties prescribed
by law and as may be assigned by City Council.”

In 2020, the City initiated a Request for Proposals (RFP) process to identify a consultant
to perform the City Treasurer functions outlined in the MMC. After reviewing the proposal
and qualifications of Ruth F. Quinto, the City entered into a two-year agreement, followed
by two subsequent amendments which extended the agreement through November 13,
  Page 1 of 2
  Agenda Item # 3.A.
  Page 1 of 28
 2025. On January 12, 2026, the Council approved Amendment No. 3, which extended the
term through June 30, 2026. At that time, the City Council directed staff to develop and
issue an RFP for City Treasurer and Investment Advisory services and assigned the
Administration and Finance Subcommittee to review the proposals and make a
recommendation to the City Council regarding the selection of a City Treasurer.

Due to higher-priority operational demands, the RFP process was delayed. However, the
solicitation, which combined Treasury Services and Investment Advisory Services into a
single procurement, was issued on February 18, 2026. Following review, staff determined
that conducting separate procurements would better serve the City’s interests by allowing
each service to be evaluated independently. Accordingly, the original solicitation was
canceled and reissued as two separate RFPs—one for Treasury Services and one for
Investment Advisory Services—to better reflect the distinct scopes of work and encourage
broader competition. The separate RFPs were issued on May 5, 2026, and closed on May
29, 2026.

For Treasury Services, the City received four proposals. Staff evaluated the proposals
based on the stated selection criteria, including qualifications, experience, and cost. Based
on this evaluation, staff identified Ms. Ruth Quinto of Quinto Consulting LP as the proposer
that best aligns with the City’s needs and recommends selection of Ms. Quinto as the City
Treasurer.

Ms. Quinto is a Certified Public Accountant licensed in the State of California and has
provided treasury services to the City of Malibu from November 2020 to the present. In
this role, she has provided oversight of cash management, investment monitoring, internal
control review, and financial reporting support. Her familiarity with the City’s operational
processes, financial environment, and institutional history provides immediate continuity,
supports informed decision-making, and promotes uninterrupted service delivery.

The agreement provides for standard monthly City Treasurer services, as well as
additional on-call, hourly services as directed by the City Manager or the City Manager’s
designee, to address additional tasks and assignments as they arise throughout the year.

Treasury Services

Experience
My experience and background serve the City’s interests through a proven track record
of leadership in municipal treasury management, financial oversight, and public agency
fiscal administration.

Additionally, I am an active Certified Public Accountant licensed in the State of California.

Since November 2020 through the present, I have provided treasury services to the City
of Malibu, supporting municipal cash management, cash flow oversight, investment
monitoring, financial review processes, and internal control and reporting functions. This
experience provides continuity of institutional knowledge and familiarity with the City’s
operational and financial environment.

From August 2005 through September 2020, I served as the Chief Financial Officer for
the Fresno Unified School District, responsible for treasury management, accounting,
budgeting, debt management and fiscal policy development and implementation. I was
appointed during a period of significant fiscal distress and impending state bankruptcy.
Through disciplined financial management, the District’s finances were stabilized within
12 months and remained financially strong, including balanced budgets, clean audits,
and healthy reserves, throughout my tenure.

Prior to my time at the Fresno Unified School District, I served for eight years as a City
Controller. From May 2001 through August 2005, I served as the City Controller for the
City of Fresno, and from August 1997 through May 2001, I served as the City Controller
and Revenue Officer at the City of Moreno Valley. Both engagements included
responsibility for treasury management, accounting, budgeting, debt management, and
fiscal policy development and implementation. My experience with the City of Moreno
Valley, a contract city, is particularly relevant to the City of Malibu’s structure.

Team Organization
This proposal is submitted by Quinto Consulting, LP as an independent consulting firm.
As the primary point of contact, the City will work directly with me throughout the
engagement, ensuring consistency and responsiveness.

As Managing Partner and sole member, I will personally perform the services described
in this proposal and will remain directly responsible for coordination with City staff,
completion of deliverables, and attendance at meetings as required. I will dedicate the
time necessary to fulfill the requirements of the engagement and will serve as the sole
assigned consultant for all services under this proposal.

Project Understanding and Approach to Scope of Work
The City is seeking a consultant to serve as City Treasurer and provide treasury, cash
management, investment policy support, and financial advisory services.

My approach is to provide practical, responsive, and policy-driven treasury services
tailored to the City’s operational needs. The engagement will emphasize safeguarding
public funds, maintaining liquidity, ensuring compliance with governing statutes and
policy, and providing clear and reliable reporting. I understand the importance of timely
responsiveness and availability in supporting City operations, management, and Council
requests.

  Page 4 of 28  2|Page
 Quinto Consulting, LP
Treasury Services

Services will include, but are not limited to:

Core Treasurer Responsibilities

1. Serve as a proactive financial partner to the City staff by monitoring inflows, outflows,
  and short-term cash needs.
2. Be responsible for the safe deposit of all moneys in the custody of the City.
3. Conduct periodic review of surplus cash investments in accordance with City Council
  adopted investment policies.
4. Review warrant registers.
5. Review receipts and disbursement schedules.
6. Prepare monthly investment reports.
7. Review the City Budget.
8. Review monthly bank reconciliations.
9. Review annual independent audit and other audits as requested.
10. Conduct annual review of banking services.
11. Attend Investment Advisory Committee or City Council meetings as necessary.
12. Coordinate with City Manager, Assistant City Manager, and Financial Controller on
  City financial matters.
13. Report to the City Council as required.
14. Other duties as approved by the City Council.

Cash Management and Treasury Operations

15. Provide active, ongoing review of cash balances, bank accounts, liquidity positions,
  and treasury operations.
16. Monitor all City bank accounts for accuracy, security, and compliance with the City’s
  banking services agreement.
17. Provide alerts and recommendations regarding unusual activity, account structure
  optimization, or opportunities to reduce banking costs.
18. Advise on the timing of transfers, withdrawals, and investment purchases or
  liquidations in a manner that protects liquidity and remains consistent with safety and
  policy requirements.
19. Provide enhanced internal control and financial operations support including
  conducting detailed review of operating procedures for both check-cutting and bank
  reconciliations, ensuring accuracy, segregation of duties, and strong internal controls.
20. Recommend improvements to strengthen fraud prevention, financial transparency,
  and operational reliability.

Investment Policy, Strategy, and Market Monitoring

21. Perform a comprehensive annual review of the City’s Investment Policy.
22. Assist the City in developing a fully revised investment policy that is modern,
  compliant, and tailored to City objectives.
23. Continually monitor market conditions and circumstances and report on any
  recommended updates to policy and permitted investment practices. Propose
  additional updates based on industry best practices, regulatory changes, and risk-
  management considerations.

  Page 5 of 28  3|Page

Treasury Services

Financial Forecasting and Long-Term Planning

24. Conduct interest forecasting, including:
  a. Short-term rate projections
  b. Multi-year interest rate forecasting
  c. Sensitivity analysis to support financial planning and long-term modelling
25. Provide multi-year financial forecasting to support budget development, capital
  planning, and long-term fiscal strategy.
26. Support the City in developing, reviewing, and updating fund balance policies,
  including minimum reserve requirements, emergency reserves, disaster
  contingencies, and stabilization targets.
27. Assist the City in ensuring it is financially prepared to respond to emergencies or
  disasters, including advising on accessible liquidity, short-term borrowing strategies,
  and the sequencing of available funds.

My approach to municipal cash management is conservative and policy-based. The
primary objectives are safety of principal, liquidity sufficient to meet operational cash flow
needs, and compliance with California law and City policies. Yield considerations, while
important, remain secondary to safety, liquidity, and policy compliance.

Conflict of Interest
I currently serve as the City Treasurer for the City of Malibu.

Other than this professional relationship, I have no financial, business, or other
relationships that would create a conflict of interest with respect to this engagement. I am
not aware of any clients with a financial interest in the outcome of this contract.

Exceptions
There are no exceptions or requested changes.

Cost Proposal
Quinto Consulting LP shall be compensated at a rate of $2,500 per month for City
Treasurer services, for an annual total of $30,000.

Additional on-call services shall be billed at $250 per hour, not to exceed 40 hours
annually, or $10,000 per year. Total not-to-exceed annual cost: $40,000.

All rates are subject to a 3% annual increase during the term of the engagement.

  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

  This Professional Services Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of
July, 2026, by and between the City of Malibu, a municipal corporation (hereinafter referred to as
the "City"), and Quinto Consulting LP, a California limited partnership (hereinafter referred to as
"Consultant"). City and Consultant are herein collectively referred to as “Parties” and separately
as a “Party”.

  The City and the Consultant agree as follows:

  RECITALS

  A.  The City does not have the personnel able and/or available to perform the services
required under this Agreement.

  B.  The City desires to contract with Consultant for professional services relating to
City Treasurer Services.

  C.  The Consultant warrants to the City that it has the qualifications, experience and
facilities to perform the services under this Agreement in a proper and timely manner.

  D.  The City and the Consultant desire to enter into this Agreement for the Consultant
to perform the services described in this Agreement, including those set forth in Exhibit A.

  NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth
herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are
hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

  1.0  SCOPE OF THE CONSULTANT’S SERVICES. The Consultant agrees to
provide the services and perform the tasks set forth in Exhibit A (the “Scope of Work”), attached
hereto and made part of this Agreement, except that, to the extent that any provision in Exhibit A
conflicts with this Agreement, the provisions of this Agreement govern. The Scope of Work may
be amended from time to time by way of a written directive from the City.

  2.0  TERM OF AGREEMENT. This Agreement will become effective on July 1,
2026, and will remain in effect for a period of three years from said date unless otherwise expressly
extended and agreed to by both Parties or terminated by either Party as provided herein.

  3.0  CITY AGENT. The City Manager, or his or her designee (collectively, the “City
Manager”), for the purposes of this Agreement, is the agent for the City; whenever approval or
authorization is required, Consultant understands that the City Manager has the authority, but not
the requirement, to provide that approval or authorization.

  4.0  COMPENSATION FOR SERVICES. The City shall pay the Consultant for its
professional services rendered and costs incurred pursuant to this Agreement in accordance with
the Scope of Work’s fee and cost schedule. The cost of services shall not exceed Forty Thousand
Dollars ($40,000) per year. Beginning with the second contract year, and on each anniversary

  Page 8 of 28
 thereafter, the annual not-to-exceed compensation may be increased by up to three percent (3%)
for a total amount not to exceed $123,636 for the term of the Agreement. No additional
compensation shall be paid for any other costs or expenses incurred, unless first approved by the
City Manager in writing.

  4.1  The Consultant shall submit to the City, by no later than the 10th day of each
month, its bill for services itemizing the fees and costs incurred during the previous month. The
City shall pay the Consultant all uncontested amounts set forth in the Consultant's bill within 30

  5.0  CONFLICT OF INTEREST. The Consultant represents that it presently has no
interest and shall not acquire any interest, direct or indirect, in any real property located in the City

The Consultant further represents that in performance of this Agreement, no person having any
such interest shall be employed by it.

  5.1  The Consultant represents that no City employee or official has a material
financial interest in the Consultant’s business. During the term of this Agreement and/or as a result
of being awarded this contract, the Consultant shall not offer, encourage or accept any financial

apply to any subcontractor hired by Consultant to perform service under this Agreement.

  5.2  If a portion of the Consultant’s services called for under this Agreement
shall ultimately be paid for by reimbursement from and through an agreement with a developer of

any work for such developer/franchisee within the last twelve (12) months, and shall not negotiate,
offer or accept any contract or request to perform services for that identified developer/franchisee
during the term of this Agreement.

  6.0  GENERAL TERMS AND CONDITIONS.

  6.1  Termination.

  6.1.1 Termination Without Cause. Either the City Manager or the
Consultant may terminate this Agreement, without cause, by giving the other Party ten (10) days
written notice of such termination and the effective date thereof. If the City terminates this
Agreement without cause, the Consultant shall prepare and shall be entitled to receive
compensation pursuant to a close-out bill for services rendered and fees incurred pursuant to this
Agreement through the effective date of the notice of termination. If the Consultant terminates this
Agreement without cause, the Consultant shall be paid only for those services completed in a
manner satisfactory to the City.

  6.1.2 Termination For Cause. If the Consultant or the City fail to fulfill

such termination and specifying the effective date of such termination. The Consultant shall be
entitled to receive compensation in accordance with the terms of this Agreement for any work

 satisfactorily completed hereunder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Consultant shall not be

  6.1.3 In the event of any termination hereunder, all finished or unfinished documents,

  6.3  Non-Discrimination. The Consultant shall not discriminate as to race,

Subject:  Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Signal Synchronization Project

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Provide a recommendation to the City Council to appropriate
$1,250,000 in Account No. 310-9066-5100 (PCH Signal Synchronization System
Improvements Project).

FISCAL IMPACT:
An additional appropriation is required. Funding for this project is included in the Adopted
Budget for Fiscal Year 2026-2027 in Account No. 310-9066-5100 (PCH Signal
Synchronization System Improvements Project).

This project is funded through Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
(Metro) Measure R and Measure M allocations in the amount of $19,100,000. Additionally,
this project was impacted by the Palisades Fire, City staff are working with the Federal
Highway Administration (FHWA) for potential reimbursement up to $246,000.

The project expenses, design, construction, and contingencies include a total amount of
$20,596,000; this amount incorporates the costs associated with PCH Signal
Synchronization, Safety Adaptive, Speed Enforcement Systems, in addition to other safety
enhancements. The estimated budget for the Speed Enforcement Systems is currently
$2.1 Million. However, the current funds are insufficient to complete the installation of the
speed enforcement systems and its components; an additional $1,250,000 is required to
complete the project.

The appropriation in the amount of $1,250,000 will support:
  • Construction costs in the amount of $900,000 to complete power source
  connections to operate the speed enforcement systems. Change Order to GMZ to
  perform work will only occur if an appropriation is approved.
  • Amendment to Kimley-Horn's agreement in the amount of $108,000 for support
  services. Additional services were needed from Kimley-Horn to modify the design
  plans and perform structural calculations to determine if the equipment provided
  could sustain the loads now required. This work was needed to obtain Caltrans’
  approval and issuance of the encroachment permit.
  • SCE contracts and invoices for energization (approx. $75,000) until transfer to a
  new account code takes place. To energize the systems, SCE contracts and
  invoices for new service connections will need to be paid and range in varying
  amounts depending on region and work (typical for new service processes).
  • The remainder of money is not anticipated to be expended, rather it's to provide

Staff are requesting to utilize the General Fund to offset the funding shortfall to
successfully complete the installation of the Speed Enforcement Systems. The Speed
System is being installed per Senate Bill 1297, which states under section 22436,
"Revenues derived from any program utilizing a speed safety system for speed limit
enforcement shall first be used to recover program costs. Program costs include, but are

 not limited to, the installation of speed safety systems, the adjudication of violations, and
reporting requirements as specified in this section". The appropriation of $1,250,000 is
reimbursable to the city and sees first recovery from the revenues of the program.

Seeking additional allocations from Metro would take approximately 12 months, in which
all work would need to halt until an approval is received. This timeframe would greatly
impact the project by significantly reducing city’s participation in the program as its sunset
date per the bill is January 1, 2032. This delay would also result in the City not receiving
estimated revenues of $4.5 Million.

Therefore, staff recommend an appropriation to this project in the amount of $1,250,000
from the General Fund Undesignated Reserves to Account No. 310-9066-5100 (PCH
Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project) for a total revised project budget
of $20,596,000.

STRATEGIC PRIORITY: This item supports the City’s 2025-2028 Strategic Plan Goal 4:
Improve Public Safety.

Goal 4: Improve Public Safety
Objective 4.1: Reduce injury and fatal collisions on Pacific Coast Highway
Strategy: Installation of speed enforcement systems

DISCUSSION: The Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) Signal Synchronization System
Improvements project (Project) has the objective of enhancing and improving traffic
signals throughout the Malibu PCH corridor; which reduces congestion, regulates vehicle
speeds, improves intersection performance, and enhances safety for motorists,
pedestrians, cyclists, and transit users. Spanning approximately eight miles from Topanga
Canyon Boulevard to John Tyler Drive, the project includes: upgrading traffic signal
hardware and controllers, installing fiber optic communication infrastructure, deploying
CCTV cameras, establishing real-time communication with Caltrans District 7 Traffic
Management Center, implementing coordinated signal timing and adaptive safety
technology.

On February 27, 2023, the City Council approved a construction agreement with GMZ
Engineering, Inc. for the PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project.

Following the tragic October 2023 fatal crash involving four Pepperdine University
students, the City expanded the project scope to include the installation of speed
enforcement systems along PCH to address the growing concerns of safety on PCH. Staff
were directed to proceed with a layout and design of a speed enforcement system.

On September 23, 2024, the City Council approved Amendment No. 5 to the Professional
Services Agreement with Kimley-Horn for the PCH Signal Synchronization System
Improvements Project; which included assistance to prepare a plan for the placement and
design of the speed enforcement systems.

  Page 3 of 4
  Agenda Item 3.B.
  Page 27 of 28
 On June 16, 2025, the City of Malibu Planning Commission approved Coastal
Development Permit No. 25-024 to install speed enforcement systems at 5 regions along
PCH.

On April 13, 2026, the City Council approved a Professional Services Agreement with Blue
Line Solutions-CA, LLC (Blue Line) to implement and operate a Speed Safety Camera
System Pilot Program. After which, it was discovered that the initial design required
modification to be aligned with the performance ability of the vendor’s camera system and
Senate Bill 1297. The level of construction effort needed to address these design
modifications and successfully install and operate the systems was much more extensive
than the available project budget. Most specifically, it was discovered that hard power
connections were required for all poles - the cost of supplying hard power connections is
the bulk of the appropriation needed.

Staff recommends the Administrative and Finance Subcommittee provide a
recommendation to the City Council to appropriate $1,250,000 in Account No. 310-9066-
5100 (PCH Signal Synchronization System Improvements Project).
